paragraphs: The European Union needs money for its next long-term budget. This budget will run from 2028 to 2034.
António Costa leads the European Council. He wants a new tax on very big tech companies. The tax would be 3% of some of their online income. It could bring in about €35 billion in seven years.
Costa also wants a smaller budget than first planned. He cut it by about €180 billion.
Taoiseach Micheál Martin says Ireland does not support the tax. He thinks tax rules for the whole world should be agreed by the whole world.
EU leaders will meet on 26 and 27 November. All countries must agree before the tax can start.
sentZh: 歐盟的下一個長期預算需要資金。
這個預算將從2028年執行到2034年。
安東尼奧・科斯塔領導歐洲理事會。
他想對非常大型的科技公司課徵一項新稅。
這項稅將是他們部分網路收入的3%。
它在七年內可帶來約350億歐元。
科斯塔也希望預算比原先計畫的小。
他把預算刪減了約1800億歐元。
總理米歇爾・馬丁表示愛爾蘭不支持這項稅。
他認為全球的稅務規則應由全世界共同決定。
歐盟領袖將於11月26日和27日開會。
所有國家都必須同意，這項稅才能開始實施。

paragraphs: The President of the European Council, António Costa, has suggested a new EU tax on large digital companies to help pay for the EU's next long-term budget. The budget will cover the years 2028 to 2034.

The tax would be 3% of money earned from online advertising, digital marketplaces and selling user data. It would only apply to companies that earn more than €750 million around the world and more than €50 million from digital services in the EU. Experts think it could raise about €35 billion over seven years.
Costa also cut the size of the budget from €1.76 trillion to €1.58 trillion, after Germany asked for lower spending. Money for competitiveness and security fell the most.
Taoiseach Micheál Martin said Ireland does not support the digital tax. He said global taxes should be agreed at a global level. Many large tech firms have their European offices in Ireland.
EU leaders will discuss the plan at a summit on 26 and 27 November. Every member state must agree before any new tax can be introduced.
sentZh: 歐洲理事會主席安東尼奧・科斯塔提議對大型數位公司課徵新的歐盟稅，以協助支付歐盟下一個長期預算。
這個預算將涵蓋2028年到2034年。
這項稅將是線上廣告、數位市集和出售用戶資料所得收入的3%。
它只適用於全球收入超過7.5億歐元、且在歐盟數位服務收入超過5000萬歐元的公司。
專家認為它在七年內可籌得約350億歐元。
在德國要求降低支出後，科斯塔也把預算規模從1.76兆歐元削減到1.58兆歐元。
用於競爭力和安全的資金減少最多。
總理米歇爾・馬丁表示愛爾蘭不支持這項數位稅。
他說全球性的稅應在全球層面上達成協議。
許多大型科技公司的歐洲辦公室設在愛爾蘭。
歐盟領袖將在11月26日和27日的高峰會上討論這項計畫。
任何新稅推出前，每個成員國都必須同意。

paragraphs: European Council President António Costa has revived the idea of an EU-wide digital services tax as part of a compromise plan for the bloc's next long-term budget, which runs from 2028 to 2034.

The levy would be set at 3% of revenue from online advertising, digital marketplaces and the monetisation of user data. It would target firms with global turnover above €750 million and EU digital revenue above €50 million, and it is expected to raise around €35 billion over seven years.

At the same time, Costa reduced the overall budget from the Commission's proposed €1.76 trillion to €1.58 trillion, a cut of roughly 10%. Germany had led calls for lower spending, and funding for competitiveness and security took the biggest hit.

Taoiseach Micheál Martin made it clear that Ireland does not back the digital tax, arguing that global taxation needs to be handled globally. The issue matters to Ireland, which hosts the European headquarters of many major technology companies.
Leaders will debate the proposal at a summit on 26 and 27 November, but any new tax would require the unanimous approval of all member states.
sentZh: 歐洲理事會主席安東尼奧・科斯塔重提全歐盟數位服務稅的構想，作為歐盟下一個長期預算（2028至2034年）妥協方案的一部分。
這項稅將定為線上廣告、數位市集及用戶資料變現收入的3%。
它將針對全球營業額超過7.5億歐元、歐盟數位收入超過5000萬歐元的企業，預計七年內可籌得約350億歐元。
同時，科斯塔將整體預算從執委會提議的1.76兆歐元減至1.58兆歐元，削減約10%。
德國先前帶頭呼籲降低支出，而競爭力與安全的資金受到的衝擊最大。
總理米歇爾・馬丁明確表示愛爾蘭不支持數位稅，並主張全球稅務須在全球層面處理。
這個議題對愛爾蘭很重要，因為許多大型科技公司的歐洲總部都設在愛爾蘭。
領袖們將在11月26日和27日的高峰會上辯論這項提案，但任何新稅都需要所有成員國一致同意。

paragraphs: European Council President António Costa has resurrected plans for an EU-wide digital services levy, folding it into a compromise blueprint for the bloc's 2028 to 2034 budget.

The charge would amount to 3% of revenue derived from online advertising, digital marketplaces and the monetisation of user data. It would apply only to firms with a global turnover exceeding €750 million and EU digital revenue of more than €50 million, and it is projected to yield some €35 billion over seven years.

In a bid to placate fiscally cautious capitals led by Berlin, Costa also pared back the Commission's €1.76 trillion proposal to €1.58 trillion. Spending on competitiveness and security bore the brunt of the reductions.

Taoiseach Micheál Martin swiftly signalled Ireland's opposition, insisting that global taxation must be tackled on a global footing. The stakes are high for Ireland, which is home to the European headquarters of numerous tech giants.
Leaders are due to thrash out the proposal at a summit on 26 and 27 November, yet any new tax would require unanimity, effectively handing each member state a veto.
